title: NanoFLUX: Distillation-Driven Compression of Large Text-to-Image Generation Models for Mobile Devices
claim: A large teacher architecture is compressed into a much smaller student by pruning blocks, downsampling tokens, and swapping components, shown side by side.
layout: 2 side-by-side architecture diagrams, bottom-to-top flow, zoomed block insets with parameter counts
description: Two vertical architecture diagrams sit side by side. The left one shows teacher FLUX.1-Schnell (17B). The right one shows the student NanoFLUX (2.4B). Data flows bottom to top. Prompt text goes through the text encoders (CLIP and T5-XXL on the left, T5-Large-Distilled on the right). The embeddings then go through a red Double-Stream block (x19) and a blue Single-Stream block (x38 on the left, x23 on the right). Green and orange token bars mark text and image tokens. The NanoFLUX stack adds purple trapezoids for a Token Downsampler and Upsampler, with a Single-Stream block between them. Dashed lines connect each block to a zoomed inset of its internals. The insets show Scale&Shift, MLP, Joint Attention, FFN and LayerNorm, with parameter counts (~140M, ~340M, ~27M, ~57M). The large titles and the bold colored blocks catch the eye first.
caption: Overview of the teacher \param{17B} FLUX.1-Schnell (left) and \param{2.4B} \name{} (right).
abstract: While large-scale text-to-image diffusion models continue to improve in visual quality, their increasing scale has widened the gap between state-of-the-art models and on-device solutions. To address this gap, we introduce NanoFLUX, a 2.4B text-to-image flow-matching model distilled from 17B FLUX.1-Schnell using a progressive compression pipeline designed to preserve generation quality. Our contributions include: (1) A model compression strategy driven by pruning redundant components in the diffusion transformer, reducing its size from 12B to 2B; (2) A ResNet-based token downsampling mechanism that reduces latency by allowing intermediate blocks to operate on lower-resolution tokens while preserving high-resolution processing elsewhere; (3) A novel text encoder distillation approach that leverages visual signals from early layers of the denoiser during sampling. Empirically, NanoFLUX generates 512 x 512 images in approximately 2.5 seconds on mobile devices, demonstrating the feasibility of high-quality on-device text-to-image generation.
